title.narrative: 1.2. Percentage of approved and implemented District Development Plans (PDD) and Annual plans and budgets (PESOD) supported by the programme/action that are based on inclusive participatory processes that address the needs identified, climate action and local economic development.

description.narrative: 1.2. Percentage of approved and implemented District Development Plans (PDD) and Annual plans and budgets (PESOD) supported by the programme/action that are based on inclusive participatory processes that address the needs identified, climate action and local economic development. Measures the extent to which inclusive local governance in selected provinces and conflict affected districts has improved.

comment.narrative: All 14 districts had PEDDs that included climate change resilience and local economic development promotion strategies andor actions.
PDD 14 per 4 years PESOD 14 per year x 4 years 70 total target 5270

As part of the decentralization process the districts have on their agenda the preparation of medium and shortterm local development plans such as the PEDD District Economic Development Plan and PESODs District Economic and Social Budgetary Plan.Therefore 14 PESODs were produced by the district technical teams in the 14 districts where the DELPAZ programme is implemented 1 per district which reflect the priority activities and respective financial planning by development sector. The PESODs are produced annually and the strengthening of the technical capacity of the ETDs by the DELPAZ programme has contributed to the exercise of inclusive and participatory planning as well as improved the process of execution and accountability by local governments thus ensuring the alignment of annual planning with the district development strategy PEDDs in its implementation period of 5 to 10 renewable years

As part of the Output 1 of DELPAZ programme IMD Institute for Multiparty Democracy and IFAPA Beira conducted training sessions for capacity building of target programme groups. In total IFAPA facilitated the following trainings07 training in Inclusive Local Governance for Peacebuilding with a focus on conflictaffected communities09 Trainings in Inclusion of Climate Change Resilience Actions in the Elaboration of the PESOD and PEDDs05 Training on the Methodology for Integrating the LED Approach into District Strategic PlanningIn turn IMD carried out Training of Local Actors on Social Inclusion Dialogue for Peacebuilding and Gender Empowerment. In total 715 participants were benefited 453 M 262 W which approximately 36.6 of the participants were women representing an average above the 25 expected by the programme. In general the training sessions were attended by local representatives community leaders members of local councils members of SCOs members of district technical teams former members of DRR and women. More specifically members of political parties also participated in the training facilitated by IMD.These trainings have produced visible results in strengthening governance processes by improving the organization and functioning of local councils which are essential bodies for promoting political participation and inclusion. Furthermore the trainings have strengthened the debate at regional and local levels on initiatives to integrate members covered by the DRR process as well as to consolidate peace and stability processes in the country.

comment.narrative: Within the DELPAZ the component of strengthening governance processes through the elaboration of management instruments that facilitate governance processes at different levels of the public service is one of the objectives to be reinforced within the programme. Thus two guidelines were produced to guide governance processes in the public service namely Practical Guide for the Performance of the Public Service and Guide for the Preparation and Analysis of the Management Account.The elaboration of these guidelines is a response to the decentralization process as well is a practical tool for an easy and accessible guide to reinforce the technical capacity of public employees in the management of public processes. Due to the high turnover of public employees at district and provincial levels in Mozambique there has been a discontinuity in the management of knowledge and public processes. These guidelines will facilitate the integration of human resources into the public service as they offer a simple and practical methodology for guiding public expenditure and state management accounts thus reducing the time for integrating new staff into the public service as well as to following the processes in public management.

comment.narrative: As part of the Project Identification and Prioritization Exercise in Sofala Province a participatory investment identification exercise was carried out in the 6 districts covered by the programme in this province Chemba Cheringama Chibabava Machnaga Gorongosa and Maringue. It was the responsibility of DELPAZUNCDF in collaboration with the implementing partner ADA as well as SPEF and EDTs to ensure the support and technical assistance for the participatory and inclusive planning process in the model of project identification and prioritization to local governments. The exercise was attended by interest groups Women Youth Leaders and Civil Society represented within the local district councils.Therefore in the first stage of the participatory exercise the interest groups were trained by the technical teams on the Guide for Identification and Prioritization of Investment Projects so that they could identify and present their proposals for Local Economic Develop LED and Climate Change Adaptation CCA investment projects. These were submitted for consideration and voting by the working groups.As a result six main investment project proposals were prioritized and approved by the advisory boards in each district with an estimated budget of approximately 18400000.00 MZN Eighteen Million Four Hundred Thousand Meticals. In all districts the prioritization of projects selected by groups of women and young people was notable. Among the prioritized projects the construction of water supply systems and projects linked to food security supply of seeds and strengthening of agricultural associations stand out.

The implementing partner for the local governance component of DELPAZ IFAPA Beira conducted a study on Opportunities and experiences for promoting local governance 2021 2023 which aimed to analyse the gains from the implementation of the programme in promoting local governance and peacebuilding in the 3 provinces Sofala Tete and Manica.A qualitative and quantitative methodology was applied in the study with semistructured interviews and open questions being prepared in which representative beneficiaries of the programme were surveyed highlightingDistrict administratorsSectorial Directors Ministry of FinanceHeads of ETDHead of the PostLocal LeadersCivil SocietyBeneficiary Members of the DDR Process.Overall it was found that the implementation of the DELPAZ programme generated significant gains improving local governance processes. The approach of the trainings facilitated by the IFAPA Implementation Partners with an emphasis on building the technical capacity of local technical teams throughout the central region is an innovation brought by the DELPAZ programme. The same methodology has aroused interest from other organizations which have shown interest in replicating it in their programmes.The study found that the programme significantly promoted the LED component through the construction and rehabilitation of socioeconomic infrastructures resilient to extreme climate events with emphasis on the construction of water supply systems schools and support for food security. As a result of the good implementation of the program the different stakeholders interviewed were unanimous in agreeing that the technical capacity building methodologies carried out by the programme should in this last phase cover localities benefiting more citizens as well as collecting and disseminating the good practices of programme to guarantee the sustainability of the development actions.
